scenes.headline: How a stack of world models plans far ahead
scenes.sub: Each level predicts farther, in a latent space of its own.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Summit! Today, a world model built as a stack, where each level looks twice as far ahead.

scenes.text: Stack world models so each level predicts twice as far ahead in its own latent space, then plan from the top down.
scenes.say: Each level predicts twice as far, in its own space. Then we plan from the top down.

steps.say: Level one reads the camera and predicts its next latent, five steps ahead.
Level two reads every other level one latent, so each guess spans ten steps.
Level three spans twenty. The legs are unpredictable that far out, so it drops them and keeps the position.

parts.note: guess the next latent at this level
parts.say: Each level is graded on predicting its own next latent.

parts.note: keeps the batch shaped like a Gaussian
parts.say: A Gaussian shape test on the batch stops every level from collapsing to one point.

steps.say: The top level searches for big macro actions whose last prediction lands on the goal.
Its first predicted state becomes the subgoal for the level below.
Level one finds motor actions that reach it, runs a couple, and the stack replans.

left.title: Flat planner
left.say: A flat planner rolls one model far ahead, and its distance to the goal stays flat until it is close.

right.title: Hierarchy
right.say: The hierarchy plans short hops, and measures distance where it grades along the corridors.

scenes.title: Visual AntMaze, three levels
scenes.say: On the ant maze, success goes from eighteen percent to seventy three. A hierarchy that shares one space gets thirty nine.

scenes.text: Ask a level to predict farther and it forgets what it cannot predict. What remains is the slow part worth planning with.
scenes.say: Predict farther, and a level forgets what it cannot predict. What remains is the slow part worth planning with.

recap: Each level predicts twice as far
SIGReg keeps every level from collapsing
scenes.say: Each level predicts twice as far. A Gaussian test keeps them apart. Plans flow down as subgoals.
